### From Bubble Sort to Odd-Even Sort {#sec-odd-even}

Bubble sort applies the comparison and swap to two elements in a vector, then uses its updated vector in the next comparison. In FHE we have a unique advantage, that being the vectorwide nature of comparisons, computations batched on an entire ciphertext are functionally of the same cost as two individual operations. Using this, we can organize the comparisons into layers of disjoint pairs, where each layer is a single vectorwide comparison and swap. This is called odd-even sort. It is a simple example of optimizations that can be made to bubble sort, and is a stepping stone to more advanced sorting networks.

Odd-even sort, also called odd-even transposition sort, organizes the comparisons into two alternating layers [^improvements-1]. Number the vector positions from $1$. The **odd layer** compares

$$
(1,2),\ (3,4),\ (5,6),\ldots,
$$

and the **even layer** compares

$$
(2,3),\ (4,5),\ (6,7),\ldots.
$$


For one iteration, let the input be $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_{n/2})$, with $n/2$ even. In the odd layer, compare-and-swap the disjoint pairs $(x_1,x_2)$, $(x_3,x_4),\ldots,(x_{n/2-1},x_{n/2})$ simultaneously. Write the resulting vector as

$$
x'=(a_1,b_1,a_2,b_2,\ldots,a_{n/4},b_{n/4}),
$$

where $(a_k,b_k)=(\min(x_{2k-1},x_{2k}),\max(x_{2k-1},x_{2k}))$ for $k=1,\ldots,n/4$. Then the even layer compare-and-swaps $(b_1,a_2),(b_2,a_3),\ldots,(b_{n/4-1},a_{n/4})$ simultaneously, leaving the endpoints in place. This produces the next vector

$$
x''=(a_1,c_1,d_1,c_2,d_2,\ldots,c_{n/4-1},d_{n/4-1},b_{n/4}),
$$

where $(c_k,d_k)=(\min(b_k,a_{k+1}),\max(b_k,a_{k+1}))$ for $k=1,\ldots,n/4-1$. One odd layer followed by one even layer is one odd-even iteration; repeating this fixed schedule moves values toward their sorted positions.

Repeat the alternating layers for $N$ phases to sort $N$ inputs. Sequentially, bubble sort performs $O(N^2)$ individual compare and swaps, but Odd-even sort instead needs only $O(N)$ **comparison layers**, due to only requiring one vector-wide comparison-polynomial evaluation per pass, regardless of how many pairs are being compared. 

[^improvements-1]: N. Habermann, **Parallel neighbor-sort (or the glory of the induction principle)**, available from https://kilthub.cmu.edu/articles/journal_contribution/Parallel_neighbor-sort_or_the_glory_of_the_induction_principle\_/6608258?file=12099395

For the compare-and-swap operation used in each layer, see @sec-comparison-based-sorting.
